title: noisy-neighbor-triage-and-runbook-sketch
content:
Summary:

This is a working post-incident note + runbook sketch for the 2025-11-01 dedicated GPU pool degradation where a noisy-tenant workload plus an autoscaler misconfiguration produced sustained eviction storms and increased tail latency for Dedicated customers. Intent: capture timeline, quick triage checklist for on-call, suggested runbook steps for noisy neighbor isolation, and action items (both short-term mitigation and longer-term automation).

Incident impact:
- Time window: 2025-11-01 02:08 - 2025-11-01 05:12 UTC (severity: Sev2 -> Sev3 after mitigation)
- Affected customers: ~8 Dedicated clusters across us-west1 with elevated token latency and some request failures (5xx) for short-running batch jobs. No logged data loss.
- Visible symptoms: sudden increase in GPU utilization cluster-wide on a subset of nodes, KV cache thrashing, request queue growth, autoscaler launched/removes several nodes repeatedly (flapping).

Detection & Alerting:
- Alert: dedicated-gpu-pool-node-cpu/gpu-saturation fired at 02:09 (threshold was 85% GPU util for 5m).
- Secondary alert: dedicated-autoscaler-rebalance-error at 02:18 (repeated scale cycles).
- First pager: SRE on-call (Diego) at 02:12.

Initial triage notes (on-call):
- Quick check: verify metric trends on Grafana (gpu_utilization, queue_depth, token_latency_p95/p99).
- Confirmed pattern: 3 nodes (~g4dn-like) at ~98% GPU util; rest of pool 40-60%.
- Looked for model/variant spikes: Hosting logs showed a single job id 'job-tny-987' doing long-lived synchronous batches.
- Logged in to cluster via bastion (ssh jump -> kube context: dedicated-us-west1-prod).
- kubectl top nodes/pods: found 2 pods accounted for >70% of GPU on node-12.

Immediate mitigations performed:
1) Soft isolate offending pods: cordon node-12 and drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data to stop scheduling new pods (02:32).
2) Scale down offending ReplicaSets for the tenant to reduce pressure (02:40) after confirming customer SLAs and coordination via #dedicated-ops Slack thread.
3) Temporarily increase autoscaler stabilizationWindow (config bump) to 10m to prevent flapping (02:55).
4) Applied a rate-limit policy via service-mesh layer for the tenant's route to limit concurrent batch workers (03:05).
Result: queue depth decreased and tail latency improved over next 30 min; autoscaler stopped rapid oscillation by 03:20.

Root cause hypothesis (notes):
- Primary: Noisy tenant running high-concurrency synthetic batch workload that held the GPU for extended sequences causing KV cache pressure and blocking shorter-serving requests (no preemption).
- Secondary: Autoscaler misconfiguration had too-low stabilization window + aggressive scale-down threshold (scaleDownCoolOff=30s), so when the noisy job completed/failed the autoscaler removed nodes rapidly and then added them again on bursts -> eviction storms and pod churn.
- Tertiary: Lack of fast noisy-tenant detection and lack of per-tenant GPU share limits in Dedicated pools.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Pod-level GPU usage traced to tenant id tny-987; logs show contiguous 30+ minute sessions of continuous token generation with max_batch_size=64 and keepalive.
- Autoscaler logs show scaleDown events at 02:22, 02:28, 02:34 then immediate scaleUp events at 02:30, 02:36 indicating flip-flop.
- Prometheus histogram of per-pod GPU time shows heavy right skew for pods of that tenant.

Known unknowns / open questions:
- Did scheduling constraints cause certain nodes to receive disproportionate pods? (node affinity or custom tolerations)
- Was there a recent deploy that changed job concurrency semantics for that tenant? (link PR: gh://redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1290)
- Why didn't prefix/KV cache share limit protect other sessions? Need to trace cache eviction counters.

Runbook draft: Noisy neighbor triage (quick checklist for on-call)
- 0) Initial checks (first 5 minutes):
  - Confirm alerts and affected clusters (Grafana + PagerDuty).
  - Post short summary in #dedicated-ops with cluster, symptoms, and paging status.
- 1) Identify hot pods:
  - kubectl get pods -n dedicated --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount OR use custom script gpu-pod-usage.sh (see repo infra/tools).
  - query metrics: sum by(pod) (rate(gpu_compute_seconds_total[1m])) and order.
- 2) Isolate quickly:
  - cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m to stop new scheduling.
  - If pod is single-tenant use kubectl scale deployment/<d> --replicas=0 (notify customer via CS) OR kubectl delete pod/<pod> to kill immediate workload.
- 3) Stabilize autoscaler:
  - Edit HPA/ClusterAutoscaler config: increase scaleDownCooldown and stabilizationWindow to >=10m for affected ASG.
  - If cluster autoscaler logs show flapping, temporarily pause autoscaler (scale down autoscaler controllers) and manage nodes manually.
- 4) Short-term QoS controls:
  - Apply per-tenant gpu-shares via resourceQuota or isolate via nodeSelector and taints for best-effort tenants.
  - Use Istio/Envoy rate limit to cap concurrent batch workers (example: envoy rate limit: 200 concurrent for route /generate).
- 5) Validate & observe:
  - Ensure token_latency_p95/p99 trending down; watch eviction_count, kube_pod_container_status_restarts, and node_gpu_utilization.
  - Wait 30-60 min for system to stabilize.
- 6) Post-incident: revert temporary blocks only after confirming stabilization and add notes to incident ticket.

Operational runbook snippets (commands & tips):
- Top GPU-using pods (promql): topk(10, sum by(pod,namespace) (rate(gpu_compute_seconds_total[1m])))
- Eviction history: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted -A --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50
- Autoscaler logs (GKE): gcloud logging read "resource.type=k8s_cluster AND logName=projects/redwood/logs/cluster-autoscaler" --limit 200 --project redwood-prod
- Quick isolation: kubectl annotate pod/<pod> redwood/isolated=true && move pod to node with taint dedicated=isolated:NoSchedule (script: infra/tools/isolator.sh <pod>)

Proposed long-term mitigations (prioritized):
1) Per-tenant GPU share enforcement (MVP): implement resourcequota-like abstraction at scheduler level to limit per-tenant GPU allocation. Owner: Claire (deadline 2026-01-15).
2) Autoscaler safety defaults: change global config: scaleDownCooldown >= 10m, minStabilizationWindow 5m for all Dedicated pools. Owner: Ethan (deadline 2025-12-01).
3) Noisy-tenant detection alert: create alert noisy-tenant-risk when single tenant uses >40% of pool GPU for >10m. Owner: Diego (deadline 2025-12-10).
4) Fast-path isolation tooling: single command isolator.sh that taints+drains and applies rate-limits to tenant routes. Owner: infra/tools team (PR 1287).
5) Telemetry addition: log per-tenant KV cache evictions and expose as metric kv_cache_evictions_by_tenant. Owner: serving-runtime team (investigate by 2025-12-20).
6) Customer SLAs & communication: add guided config for customers on how to set concurrency limits for Dedicated jobs (docs + console wizards). Product owner: Priya (2026-02-01).

Action items (short list):
- [Amina] Create noisy-tenant alert (on-call runbook) and add to Grafana dashboard. Due: 2025-11-10.
- [Diego] Draft autoscaler safe defaults RFC and run config change in staging. Due: 2025-11-24.
- [Claire] Prototype resource quota enforcement doc and spike design. Due: 2025-12-08.
- [Ethan] Add unit tests for isolator.sh and put CI gate on infra/tools. Due: 2025-11-30.
- [CS] Notify affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps. Due: 2025-11-03.

Retro notes / learnings:
- We had good visibility at the metric level but lacked a short-circuit detection for single-tenant pressure.
- Autoscaler defaults are optimized for general workloads, not for the highly-bursty Dedicated tenant model. We should have a separate autoscaler profile for Dedicated pools.
- The on-call runbook helped reduce time-to-isolate to ~20 minutes, but automations could cut that to <5.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Could we instrument a per-tenant token-meter (per-minute GPU-seconds) and surface it in console? Useful for both SRE and customers.
- Consider a "soft-reservation" concept where customers declare peak concurrency and we enforce fair share during bursts.
- Investigate using MIG or MPS GPU partitioning for noisy tenants where hardware supports it as quick isolation layer.

Appendix: raw triage logs (sanitized):
[02:22:14] autoscaler: scaleDown group=dedicated-us-west1 delta=-3 reason=underutilized
[02:28:02] kube: evicted pod tny-987-worker-5 reason=NodePressure
[02:30:45] autoscaler: scaleUp group=dedicated-us-west1 delta=3 reason=cpu_utilization
[02:32:08] oncall Amina: cordon node-12
[03:05:12] applied envoy rate-limit to tenant tny-987 route -> concurrent=150

Next steps for this doc:
- Convert to a proper postmortem (templated) once we have RCA signoff and more logs.
- Move runbook content into confluence page /docs/runbooks/dedicated/noisy-neighbor if agreed.

If you have edits or remembered details, append below (this is intentionally informal).

-- Amina
